subject: Final MAP: NovaCare benchmarking plan & variant recommendations
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novacare.com>, Procurement <procurement@novacare.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + benchmarking plan for NovaCare

Sanjay / Procurement team — attaching a working draft of the MAP and a concise benchmarking plan so we can align on scope and the close timeline. High level asks from our side: a signed MAP and a PO so we can reserve Dedicated capacity for the pilot.

Key testing objectives (short):
- Validate TTFT (time-to-first-token) and 99th percentile latency under production-like concurrency patterns.
- Measure steady-state throughput and burst behavior for up to 500 concurrent connections (we propose starting at 200 concurrency for the pilot).
- Capture quality delta across three Redwood catalog variants for your triage prompts (privacy-preserving subset of PHI redacted).

Proposed model variants (brief):
- Variant A — 7B q4_0 (quantized): lowest cost, TTFT best, quality baseline (expected lower factuality on clinical edge cases).
- Variant B — 13B q4_1 (quantized/optimized): recommended balance; 15–35% higher token cost vs A, ~20–40% better ROUGE/factual checks in our evals.
- Variant C — 70B fp16: highest-quality comparator; higher TTFT and cost, useful for heavy-compliance/elevated-accuracy flows.

Planned runbook (attached): short synthetic replay (1 day), production-replay (2 days), steady-state long-run for concurrency profiles (>= 1 hour per profile). We'll collect TTFT, p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rates, and memory utilization per GPU.

Please confirm:
1) Target 99th-latency SLO we should validate against (you listed 300ms in the RFP; is 300ms max or do we try for 200ms?).
2) Can you provide the redacted test prompt set (or give us a sample of 500 queries to run)?
3) Any specific regulatory evidence needed during pilot (SOC2 artifacts already requested in parallel).

Attachment: MAP_NovaCare_v3.pdf (MAP + milestone timeline)
Attachment: runbook_latency_sla.md (test run commands and metrics)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m to walk through the runbook. If we get sign-off this week we can spin up capacity and start the pilot next Tue (5/4).

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0124

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novacare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novacare.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + benchmarking plan for NovaCare

Ben — thanks for this. A couple of quick clarifications from our side:

- 99th-latency SLO: procurement and infra prefer a pragmatic goal. We can target 300ms p99 as a hard acceptance threshold for our chat flows, and 200ms as a stretch target you can aim for.
- Concurrency: NovaCare expects daytime peak bursts up to ~400 concurrent inference requests during clinic hours, but for the initial pilot let's scope to 200 steady concurrency and a single 5-minute burst to 400.
- PHI/test data: I can share a redacted set of 600 prompts by EOD Monday; they will be redacted but representative of edge cases.

SOC2: we have a security questionnaire in progress — our compliance lead will follow up separately.

Please include an explicit run that reports TTFT measured as service-side time from request receive to first token emitted (avg, p95, p99) so we can compare to latency budgets in our frontend.

We appreciate the variant descriptions — our clinical lead prefers Variant B for the pilot, but we want a short A vs B quality delta and the capability to fall back to C for sensitive cases.

Sanjay
Director, Product — NovaCare Health

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + benchmarking plan for NovaCare

Ben / Markus — quick internal alignment before we send the finalized MAP to Sanjay. Notes from the infra/benching side: 

- Run matrix:
  * Phase 1 (synthetic): 1k qps ramp, 10m windows at concurrency [50, 100, 200]. Collect TTFT/p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util.
  * Phase 2 (prod-replay): 3 replay runs with real redacted prompts at 200 concurrency; include 5-minute burst to 400.
  * Phase 3 (tail-latency): 1-hour steady at 200 concurrency with a low-priority background cache-warmup to simulate user session churn.

- Measurement definitions: TTFT = receive -> first byte on wire; tokens/sec measured at model output gate; error rate includes timeouts and server 5xx.
- Hardware: run on 2 x A100-style nodes for Variant B baseline; scale up to 4 nodes for Variant C to simulate realistic cost.

I'll attach the revised runbook with CLI snippets and the scripts we'll use to compute p99 TTL. Markus will template the perf summary CSV so we can share a one-page comparison.

—
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novacare.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP + snapshot benchmark results (pilot plan)

Sanjay — attaching the finalized MAP and a short perf snapshot from our initial pilot runs on the redacted prompt set you provided. Highlights and recommended next steps below.

Quick summary of pilot runs (aggregated):
- Test sets: 600 redacted prompts (mix of clinical triage and admin dialogs) run as production-replay over 48 hours.
- Concurrency profile: steady 200 concurrency with two 5-minute bursts to 400.
- Metrics collected: TTFT (avg/p95/p99), p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rate.

Key numbers (snapshot):
- Variant A (7B q4): TTFT avg 35ms, p95 120ms, p99 230ms; steady throughput 4.2k tokens/sec per GPU; estimated unit cost: low. Quality: baseline — higher hallucination on edge clinical items (5% > acceptable threshold).
- Variant B (13B q4_1): TTFT avg 48ms, p95 160ms, p99 290ms; steady throughput 3.1k tokens/sec per GPU; estimated unit cost: medium. Quality: substantive improvement on factuality (+28% F1 on our internal checks) and significantly fewer safety flags.
- Variant C (70B fp16): TTFT avg 220ms, p95 380ms, p99 640ms; steady throughput 0.9k tokens/sec per GPU; estimated unit cost: high. Highest quality; best on clinical edge but 3x cost vs B.

Observations:
- Variant B meets the 300ms p99 acceptance threshold in most runs but sits close to the limit on burst tails (p99 ~290ms). We recommend Variant B as the pilot default with an automatic fallback to A for latency-sensitive low-risk administrative flows and escalation to C for a small % of high-compliance paths (we can implement rule-based routing).
- TTFT behavior is dominated by model size and tokenization overhead; caching prefixes for repeated session prompts yields ~10–15% TTFT improvement.

Attachments: perf_summary_novacare.csv (one-line per variant with full metric columns), MAP_NovaCare_v3.pdf (signed milestone table), runbook_latency_sla.md

Next steps requested:
1) Sanjay: sign-off on Variant B as pilot baseline and approval to reserve capacity for the pilot week (we'll provision the dedicated pool on the 2 nodes/variant baseline described).
2) Procurement: share PO cadence and any legal redlines for the MAP so we can align billing dates.
3) Tech sync: we'll set a 45m pilot kickoff Wed 5/12 to review the runbook and confirm telemetry hooks.

If you want, I can annotate the perf CSV with recommended routing rules and cost projections for a 6-month production ramp.

Best —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
